title: OneDrive: improved Copilot file skills in OneDrive on the web
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licence requirement and printed controls are supported, and searches confirmed the feature-specific documentation gaps. The action rating should be review rather than prepare because no source establishes that existing behaviour changes on arrival.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The add-on licensing model reflects the published Microsoft Copilot entitlement, with Microsoft 365 E7 inclusion noted.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot is available with Microsoft 365 E7 or as an add-on for eligible commercial, US Government, and education subscription plans.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; summary; Cost and licensing; controls[1].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes general Copilot licensing for eligible commercial, US Government and education plans.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot is available with Microsoft 365 E7 or as an add-on for eligible commercial, US Government, and education subscription plans.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft documents a Microsoft Copilot licence requirement for its OneDrive integration.
claims.quote: Copilot is only available to users with a license assigned. If you remove the license from a user, the user loses access to Copilot. Integration with SharePoint in Microsoft 365 and OneDrive is a core feature in Microsoft Copilot.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; controls[1].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Separate licensing terms for these improved file skills are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot OneDrive file skills separate licensing usage charges Advanced work billing. Opened Copilot licence options, required configuration and usage-based billing overview; none specifies separate terms for these improved skills.

claims.claim: Licence assignment is available at Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is set at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site ... Use PowerShell ... Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits discovery of content from selected SharePoint sites in Copilot.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is supported only for SharePoint sites, not OneDrive sites, and does not govern these skills' use of OneDrive files.
claims.quote: You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites. It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions and accesses only content the user is authorised to access.
claims.quote: Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions. Copilot only summarizes or references content that the user is already authorized to access.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot can surface already overshared content to anyone who has access.
claims.quote: If content is already overshared, Copilot can surface it to anyone who has access.

claims.claim: A user needs both VIEW and EXTRACT rights for Copilot to summarise or return encrypted content.
claims.quote: When content is encrypted, whether by a sensitivity label or by Azure Rights Management without a label, the user must have both the VIEW and EXTRACT usage rights for Copilot to summarize or return the content.

claims.claim: With VIEW but not EXTRACT, Copilot cannot summarise the encrypted content but can return a link.
claims.quote: If the user has VIEW but not EXTRACT, Copilot doesn't summarize the content, but it can return a link so the user can open it outside Copilot.

claims.claim: New content created by Copilot from labelled items receives the highest-priority label where inheritance is supported.
claims.quote: When Copilot creates new content from labeled items, the label with the highest priority is applied to the new content, where label inheritance is supported.

claims.claim: A Microsoft Purview DLP policy for Copilot can prevent summarisation of labelled files and emails.
claims.quote: A DLP policy for Copilot can keep Copilot from summarizing labeled files and emails. Copilot can still return a link so the user can open the item outside Copilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Audit logs Copilot interactions.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Audit automatically logs Copilot interactions.

claims.claim: Copilot audit records do not contain the text of prompts or responses.
claims.quote: Audit records don't contain the text of prompts or responses. To view that text, use eDiscovery or Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) for AI.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described whether sharing through these improved skills needs confirmation.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot in OneDrive improved file skills sharing generated outputs confirmation sharing settings labels default rollout users roles. Read release-note search excerpts and roadmap; found other sharing features, not this skill's confirmation process.

claims.claim: The roadmap and Learn do not specify roles that configure these improved skills.

claims.claim: The roadmap and Learn do not specify rollout mechanics for these improved skills.

claims.claim: Licence assignment is the documented mechanism determining who holds a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Copilot is only available to users with a license assigned. If you remove the license from a user, the user loses access to Copilot.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels are configured in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: DLP policies for Copilot are configured in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy.

claims.claim: No source says these improved skills change existing behaviour on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive improved Copilot file skills 569215 web admin switch default licensing sharing confirmation Advanced work OneDrive. Opened roadmap, Copilot settings and release notes; none describes replacement of existing behaviour by these skills.

claims.where: front matter: action; Why it matters
claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits a capability with an unknown default and no source saying existing behaviour changes.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; "No source says existing behaviour changes either." The standard assigns review to a new capability with an unstated default when no source says existing behaviour will change.
claims.fix: Change action from prepare to review. The sources describe a planned capability, not an automatic replacement or change to existing behaviour.
